patterns_discovered.description: Orphaned cloud resources from years ago create persistent attack surface when not properly decommissioned
evidence: Checkout.com breach via 5-year-old legacy cloud storage - 425-596 Hacker News points
ShinyHunters criminal group gained access to third-party cloud system used in 2020
System was 'deprecated' but not fully decommissioned - credentials still active
Attack vector: Forgotten credentials and access controls from unused system
implications: Cloud resource sprawl creates security blind spots
Migration without decommissioning leaves attack surface
Service account keys and API credentials persist indefinitely
Historical data in old systems becomes liability
No decommissioning process = time bomb waiting
patterns_discovered.chained_application: CRITICAL - Audit all GCP resources (Storage, Cloud Run, Service Accounts)
patterns_discovered.note: Direct threat - Chained likely has test/dev resources not cleaned up

evidence: TLDR DevOps: 95% orgs have 20% endpoint coverage gap
N-able Convergence Blueprint: Unified people, processes, technology
Root cause: Vaguely defined responsibilities between IT and Security
Solution: Cloud-native security platforms with AI-powered detection
implications: Traditional organizational silos create blind spots
AI enables automated threat detection at scale
Modern approach: Single pane of glass for infrastructure + security
Convergence is industry best practice, not just trend
patterns_discovered.chained_application: Extend error-observer to security events (security-observer service)
patterns_discovered.note: Natural fit for A2A architecture - security as first-class messages

Schedule quarterly security review calendar event

architecture_patterns.observation: Cloud resources require explicit decommissioning process, not just deprecation

Remove IAM bindings and access controls
automation_opportunities: Automated cleanup for test/dev resources after 30 days idle
